decision: EXP14A g002 (S3): a single RoboDojo episode may run on an official layout k of eval_seed 0 other than layout 0. A contract record reviews layout 0 only; for a one-round, unscheduled episode this table extends a task's record, unchanged, to the listed layouts when its completion layer states no layout-0-specific fact there. A task or layout not listed is refused on any layout but the record's own. Layout schedules of persistent sessions keep the reviewed pools and contract appendices (robodojo-layout-pools-v1.json) and never read this table. v2 (2026-10-10, EXP13A VLA-skill line): the table extends the same records to layouts 5-9, the development layouts of the practice loop on RoboDojo; layouts 0-4 stay the evaluation layouts compared with the EXP14A baseline table. v3 (2026-10-20, ORA F5): the table extends the registry-v8 records of the thirteen admitted tasks v2 did not list, twelve to layouts 0-9 and sweep_blocks to layouts 0, 3, 4 and 7 (its other layouts hold four or five blocks against the contract's three), so every admitted task is audited; the 29 v2 entries are unchanged. A swap_T row binds the bytes of that task's own asset revision (the entry's assets_revision, which its record and robodojo_asset_revision.asset_revision_for name); every other row binds the table's. Practice layouts generated outside the official set are out of scope. v4 (2026-11-14, RoboDojo f57e163 and Assets 1127bda): the same tasks, rows and layout bytes, re-bound to the registry-v9 records. Every row, swap_T's included, binds the table's asset revision: 1127bda serves swap_T's layouts with the bytes of the retired 35efbc7d checkout. organize_table's entry binds its v4 completion layer, whose clause 4 follows the f57e163 instruction; the drawer unit it names is in every listed layout. robodojo-layout-pools-v1.json is now robodojo-layout-pools-v2.json.

review.by: layouts 0-4: EXP14A S3 implementation audit (Claude), 2026-10-08; layouts 5-9: EXP13A VLA-skill line audit (Claude), 2026-10-10; the thirteen v3 tasks: ORA F5 portability audit (Claude), 2026-10-20; human approval by scope in human_approval
review.method: For each listed task: read its registry-v8 completion layer, its upstream gen_instruction at the pinned revision, and the label/category/pose of every Rigid, Dynamic, Articulation, Garment and Geometry instance in layouts 0-9; a layer is portable when every count, side, ordering and fixture it states holds in each listed layout. Layouts 5-9 were checked against each layout-0-4 basis: per-category counts, every instance whose record is identical in layouts 0-4 (identical again in 5-9), and the poses and orderings the basis states (pads and empty pad, cube and cup rows, upright-block sides, tile rows, number-pad row, xylophone yaw, basket and button poses). v3 tasks, by the same criteria: their record, completion layer and gen_instruction, and every instance of layouts 0-9 read from the pinned bytes; each layout's evidence, the models only layouts 1-9 hold and the offline reach footprints are in the review record.
review.not_reviewed: Reachability of each layout's objects (the lane's scene smoke measures the scene, not task reach) and the evaluator metadata of objects that only layout k holds: the record's evaluator_dependencies hash layout 0's objects, and layout k's bytes are pinned by the asset revision preflight checks clean. For the v3 tasks the review record lists those objects and gives offline top-down footprint distances (robodojo_layout_reach) as evidence only; no scene smoke measured them.

v3_tasks.provenance: relayed by the ORA lead session (m2 pi re) through the coordinator; the user's words and the four conditions are in the review record

carried_from_v2.provenance: relayed by the ORA lead session (m2 pi re) through the coordinator
carried_from_v2.note: v2's human approval was pending; the user approved these entries separately from the thirteen v3 tasks. No consumer gates on approval (portable_layout reads only the task entries), so admission is unchanged.

v4_reissue.scope: the re-binding of every entry to its registry-v9 record and the f57e163/1127bda pins, and organize_table's v4 layer on its listed layouts; the v3 approvals above cover the rows' layouts, bytes and the unchanged contract texts
v4_reissue.requested_in: the pull request that pins RoboDojo f57e163

instruction_sources.fixed: gen_instruction returns one constant template with no placeholder at the pinned revision, so every layout renders the record's instruction; the RunSpec binds it and the worker refuses another.
instruction_sources.layout_readback: the instruction is generated from the layout's objects, so it differs per layout. The RunSpec binds the instruction the lane's scene smoke read back from the official reset of that exact layout (task_instruction in the lane gate's revalidation certificate); the worker refuses a reset whose instruction differs, as for every task.

press_by_number.basis: Buttons keep their poses in layouts 0-9 (red button0 at x -0.15, red button1 at x 0, blue button2 at x +0.15); only the number cards' values change, which the contract reads from the scene.

arrange_largest_number.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold four or five number pieces and as many pads in one row along world X; the contract names neither a count nor a digit.

push_T.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold one T block and one gray T pad at different poses; the contract is relative to the pad and the reset pose.

classify_objects.basis: Layouts 0-9 keep the three baskets at x -0.28, 0 and +0.28 and hold three category groups; the contract names no category.

align_blocks.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold three cubes and the set square at different poses; the contract names no pose.

solve_equation.basis: Layouts 0-9 lay an equation of five or six pads with one empty pad; the contract names no value, symbol or pad count.

stack_blocks_by_language.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold three blocks whose colours give the instruction's order (gen_instruction reads block_0..2 categories), so the instruction differs per layout; the contract defers the order to the instruction.

imitate_sorting_sequence.basis: Layouts 0-9 keep basket0 at (-0.40, -0.15) and basket1 at (+0.35, +0.25), which the contract's 'your basket' and 'the other basket' describe; the five objects differ.

classify_objects_by_language.basis: Layouts 0-9 keep the three baskets at x -0.28, 0 and +0.28; the instruction names each layout's cat0..cat2 categories and differs per layout; the contract defers category-to-basket to the instruction.

play_Xylophone.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold one mallet, its stand and one xylophone at different poses, the xylophone always at yaw 167-180 degrees; the contract's left-to-right order is world -X to +X.

play_tic_tac_toe.basis: Layouts 0-9 are identical in pieces and poses (five rings, four crosses, one board).

stack_blocks.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold three blocks of varying textures; the contract requires no texture order.

stack_bowls.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold three bowls of one model each; the contract names no model or pose.

general_pickup.basis: Layouts 0-9 each hold one labelled target among distractors; the instruction names the layout's target and differs per layout; the contract defers the object and distance to the instruction.

fold_clothes.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold one long-sleeved top at different poses; the contract names no garment model.

match_and_pick_from_conveyor.basis: Layouts 0-9 keep the conveyor and hold a target pair among three distractors; the contract names no object.

cover_blocks.basis: Layouts 0-9 keep the three cubes at x -0.2, 0, +0.2 and the cups in front; only which colour stands where changes, and the contract reads the left-to-right order at reset.

put_bottles_into_dustbin.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold four bottles and keep the dustbin at (-0.63, -0.10), matching the contract's 'all four bottles'.

pour_liquid_into_cup.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold one bottle and one cup (a goblet in layouts 3, 5 and 8); the contract says 'the cup'.

build_tower.basis: Layouts 0-9 keep two upright blocks on each side of world X (block1 and block5 at x < 0, block2 and block6 at x > 0: the contract's two pairs) and the longest board and roof at fixed poses; board sides vary but the contract names none.

pour_balls_into_vase.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold one cup with seven balls and one vase at different poses; the contract names no count.

make_kong.basis: Layouts 0-9 keep the standing row at y -0.15 from x -0.33 to +0.27 and the draw stack at x -0.40 (the contract's left end, world -X); only tile faces change.

insert_tubes.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold three tubes and one rack, matching 'all three tubes'.

store_laptop_and_headphones.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold the same five objects (headset model varies) at nearby poses; the headphone orientation clause is relative to the reset pose.

sort_nesting_dolls_by_size.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold five dolls, matching the contract.

fill_pen_holder.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold four pens (pen or oil_pen) and one holder, matching 'all four pens'.

deposit_coin.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold one coin on its stand and one coin bank at different poses.

organize_table.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold the same object set (models vary); the alignment clauses are relative to the reset pose.

make_toast.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold four slices in the rack and one toaster, matching the contract.

fasten_screws.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold three nuts lying flat and three screws standing upright, each nut paired with the screw of its own asset index (three distinct of 0-4 per layout); nut and screw metadata are byte-identical across indices and each index has its own colour, shared by its nut and screw; the contract names no colour, count beyond the pairs, or position.

fill_egg_holder.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold four eggs (egg/0) in one egg basket and the one egg holder (egg_holder/0, lid open) at different poses, matching 'all four eggs'; the contract names no pose.

hang_mugs.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold three mugs and the one mug rack (cup_holder/0) at the same height, yawed -22.7 to +8.9 degrees; every mug model they use carries layout 0's two handle frames, and the contract's peg directions are the rack's own, so they hold at any rack yaw.

insert_key.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold one key (key/0) lying on its side and the one lock (key_slot/0) at different poses (lock yaw -25 to +23 degrees); the contract's turn is relative to the keyhole's slit.

pack_objects_into_box.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold one car, electric toothbrush, hammer and shoe, each a task-config variant whose front end review-v3 identified, and box/0 upright with its long side within 24.4 degrees of world X at reset, inside the evaluator's allowance, so the box starts as the contract says it must stay.

pick_from_conveyor_by_image.basis: Layouts 0-9 keep the conveyor and the basket (basket_grasp/2) and hold one target among three distractors; the board's image is the photo Geometry/photo/map.json pairs with that layout's target model, and no distractor is that model; the contract names no object.

play_stacking_toy.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold the one peg base (stack_base/0) and ten pieces in sets of four, three, two and one, each set one model and the four models distinct; the contract identifies sets by size and pegs by height, never by colour or model.

plug_in_charger.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold one charger (charger/0) lying flat and one power strip (socket/0) at different poses; the contract names no outlet or pose.

pour_by_language.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold three bottles of three distinct colours (wine_bottle 0-2), each holding its own liquid, and three bowls of three distinct colours (wine_bowl 0-2) in permuted slots; gen_instruction names each layout's colours, so the instruction differs per layout; the contract defers the pairing to the instruction's colours and order.

store_tools_in_toolbox.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold the same four tools (hammer/5, pliers/0, tape_measure/0, wrench/0) and toolbox/0 with orientations identical to layout 0's (rotate_rand false); only positions change, and the contract is relative to the reset pose.

swap_T.basis: Layouts 0-9 hold the red T (t/0) and the blue T (t/1) lying flat at different poses; the contract is relative to the reset poses.

swap_blocks.basis: Layouts 0-9 keep the three mats and the button at layout 0's poses and hold the two identical blocks (cube/3) on two different mats; which mat is empty varies, and the contract names no mat.

sweep_blocks.basis: Layouts 0, 3, 4 and 7 hold three blocks, the dustpan lying flat and the broom, matching 'all three blocks'; layouts 1, 2, 5, 6, 8 and 9 hold four or five blocks and are not listed, so the record stays refused there.
